original_card.question: Can the proposed P104 joint endpoint flags be realized by a chronological correction program with coefficients, dirty restoration and an affordable complete bill?
methods: Construct one side-correction word at an explicit chronological cut with the needed frames still available.
Derive a lower bound on the side correction and hosting costs that decides whether this channel can beat the selected budget.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An exact arbitrary-input identity, source/target frame availability and restoration at the chosen cut, plus the complete channel+correction+idle/hosting bill or an explicit favorable bound. The native channel alone is not a supplier. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the revision-6 family record and #2981 static joint flags, alongside the reviewed #1991 channel. #2981 is an author-checked source archive, not an independently validated executable correction or a refutation of program-level lifetime floors.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: After checking live handoffs, pin one named collection from #2981 and attach acquisition/delivery times, source dependencies and coefficient requirements. Test legal access and arbitrary dirty restoration; price any completion against the full channel/endpoint/hosting allowance. Stop with the exact missing implication or a scoped counterexample rather than expanding the static cover census.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Completing an already realized changed channel tests a concrete construction opportunity, instead of refining the incumbent packing. A positive local result still needs global and all-size admission.
allowed_variations: One correction factorization, one chronological cut, or one explicit hosting obstruction.
A changed correction schedule with an updated full bill and native frame contract.
scope_change_triggers: Recompiling the already certified low-rank channel without closing a new obligation.
Treating a pending ancestor, local histogram or unpriced side correction as an admitted global supplier.
Repeating a correction or physical conversion already supplied by a pending follow-up without adding independent coverage or a different unresolved obligation.
Repeating the 208-flag static matching or calling a static nested cover a chronological correction program. Independent audit of that certificate is distinct and remains useful.

existing_checks.scope: PR #2981 reports static joint endpoint flags and a matching of 208 departure and arrival flags; archival intake is not independent verification.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent flag check and a chronological coefficient program with dirty restoration and a complete cost.

actual_scope: Pin matched present-head flag 43 (X21 to Y59, basis head 15) from the #2981 certificate and prove on the published #1991 channel that the basis head enters Y59's frame, both as a listed vector and in the GF(2) span, only at Y59's terminal transport after-frame (event 3525), after all fifteen Y59 row updates have run in head-free charts, while X21's span keeps the head at every annotation. Also certify that Y59's last two updates (events 3231 and 3364) run in charts that already span non-head basis vectors of the same flag ({32}, then {6, 18, 32}) while X21's live rank-9 frame spans them too. No Y59 event occurs while both endpoint frames host the head direction, so chronological dirty restoration cannot use co-hosted basis-head geometry on this word, even though co-hosted non-head basis geometry exists at the last two updates.
scope_change_reason: Open #3349 registers the 208-flag restoration census and names the present-head class (0, 1, 9, 43). Open #3443 pins flag 9 literally; open #3451 pins flag 1 literally and in span and asks, as its second open question, whether flag 43 follows the same span pattern. Open #3392 pins absent-head flag 2. Open #3363 and its follow-ups cover algebraic coefficient delivery, concentrated on flag 0, which is excluded. Flag 43 is the last uncertified present-head member outside the coefficient cascade. Its chronology (drop 570, arrive 3525, gap 2955) differs from flag 1 (591, 3473, 2882) and flag 9 (500, 3489, 2989), its target has fifteen updates and six transports, and its preterminal target charts host part of the flag basis, which neither prior records. Both scanners refuse to admit a chronology equal to either published prior.
bottleneck_link: A present-head target final does not host the basis-head direction while the target is still being updated, even when the target's charts already host other basis directions of the same flag. On flag 43 every Y59 row update precedes the head's entry into Y59's span, and Y59 has no event after that entry, so a dirty restoration using co-hosted head geometry needs new target events or an earlier head step.
stop_rule: Stop after flag 43's late-only hosting obstruction and its tail co-hosting are pinned literally and in span and dual-scanned. Do not build a correction word, recompute algebraic relays or coefficients, or re-certify flags 0, 1 or 9.
evidence: Flag 43 is source 21, target 59, basis head 15. X21 starts at [15]; its first transport at event 570 goes to [3, 4, 8, 128, 256], removing 15 from the list but not from the span (15 = 3 xor 4 xor 8). All 22 X21 annotations span the head and X21 is never an add destination. Y59's preterminal frames are [], [500], [127, 500], [447, 127, 52], [95, 447, 32, 20] and [95, 447, 6, 32, 20], whose spans exclude 15. The head enters Y59 only in the after-frame of event 3525, Y59's last event, with a rank-3 step (literal gap 2955 after event 570). Y59's fifteen adds (events 223-227, 2099, 2191, 2275, 2341, 2393, 2698, 2891, 3076, 3231, 3364) all run in head-free charts, ten of them in the empty chart. The adds at 3231 and 3364 run in charts spanning the non-head basis vectors {32} and {6, 18, 32}, which X21's live rank-9 frame also spans. No joint X21/Y59 event and no endpoint zero/copy/erase event exist; X21's four events after 3525 are reads. All eleven endpoint transports are nested upward with rank steps equal to their recorded costs. Neither endpoint frame is restored (ranks 1 to 9 and 0 to 8). Selected kappa is unchanged.
author: Wentao Li
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance for derivation, implementation, checking and writing.

open_questions.question: Can a changed schedule place 15 in Y59's span at or before Y59's last row update (event 3364), while X21 is still live, and what does that add to the channel bill?
open_questions.why_it_matters: On flag 43 the head is one rank step from the last preterminal chart: Y59's terminal step at event 3525 has rank 3, and the chart at 3364 already hosts the tail directions {6, 18, 32}. Moving one direction of the terminal step earlier is the smallest schedule change that would give a co-hosted head chart at a target update.
open_questions.first_step: Replace the rank-1 transport at event 3363 by a rank-2 transport whose after-frame spans 15 inside Y59's final span, keep the 3525 transport nested with rank step 2, and check the common-chart requirement against D17's frame at the add at event 3364.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package reads only the published frames of flag 43. It does not construct a repair, price one, or check D17's frame contract or any coefficient.

open_questions.question: Is tail-before-head hosting (a target update whose chart spans non-head basis vectors of the matched flag but not its head) specific to flag 43 among the four present-head flags, and does it occur on absent-head flags?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If the target typically hosts part of the flag basis before the head, the present-head obstruction is a head-specific scheduling property rather than a consequence of the target filling late; a repair then only needs to move the head step, not build the target chart.
open_questions.first_step: Run this package's tail_in_span scan on the target updates of flags 1 and 9 and of absent-head flag 2 as a separate census, citing #3451, #3443 and #3392 rather than re-certifying their chronology. #3451's certificate already records Y7's largest preterminal span {0, 95, 441, 486}, which contains none of flag 1's basis vectors.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package certifies flag 43 only. Flags 1, 9 and 2 are the subjects of open #3451, #3443 and #3392.
